# MakeUp B14 duplicate MRT write — private source candidate R1

**Private source candidate, no runtime/mod-control/performance acceptance.**
The candidate retains c2's RT3 history output, omits its duplicate RT1 output,
and aliases final's image sampling to current RT3. RT1 allocation and c2's draw
remain. No AA, native quality option, preset, scene or cloud setting is changed.
This is distinct from the closed unchanged B16 cloud-saturation trial.

Evidence is frozen under
`dev/logs/cross-shader-performance-r1/makeup-mrt-r1/`: `audit.json`, fresh pinned
Iris disassembly, `candidate.diff`, source-only conditional fixtures, original
100-option map, two archives/sidecars, integration proposal and final manifest.
The builder/audit `audit.py` reads the original ZIP afresh; all archive members
and exact renderer classes are hashed in the audit. No build/client/GPU/encoder
was started. No live jobs are owned.

## Pins and legal provenance

MakeUp UltraFast 9.5g original ZIP SHA-256 is
`0036da17e0c7158e1c669593e6322d53fce3f5a42fb5124b935e9e21a5719db8`.
Its existing recipe records release id `pgb0JjoN`, Modrinth primary/release URLs
and LGPL-3.0-or-later. Native wrappers attribute Javier Garduño and GNU LGPL v3.
`LICENSE` SHA-256 is
`e3a994d82e644b03a792a930f574002658412f62407f5fee083f2555c5f23118`.
Candidate keeps every license/readme/native configuration/property byte and
all wrapper attribution; only two common fragments change. Private archives
are ignored local artifacts, with no publication or redistribution action.

Iris NeoForge 1.8.12 + MC 1.21.1 JAR is
`3e3f94d2d5cdcb8145c4385d521974aa2d8669b2cc212351f70cf06488182e83`.
No support is inferred for other Iris/loaders/MC versions. The native-equivalent
control is a byte-for-byte original ZIP, not an unrelated adapter or new AA path.
Off and QUALITY must restore/select that original graph through the root's
transaction. The separate proposal-only 0/1 shader switch demonstrates disabled
source equivalence; it is deliberately absent from emitted archives and adds no
native shader option or runtime-uniform claim.

## Complete bounded source lifetime

The earlier R4 no-clear coverage gap has a concrete source resolution:
**prepare is an unconditional fullscreen producer before gbuffers**. All root,
world0, world1 and world-1 prepare wrappers define SET_FOG_COLOR, include
common/prepare_fragment, and its final write helper selects DRAWBUFFERS:17.
The fragment has no RT1 input or discard; its vertex uses the native fullscreen
quad MVP. Native properties have no prepare enable, scale, size or flip override.
Exact Iris pipeline shares one BufferFlipper through prepare, deferred and
composite; renderShadows invokes prepare even when its shadowRenderer is null.
RT1's old c2 result is therefore overwritten before any next-frame RT1 sampling.
Geometry/DH discard coverage is not used to certify this overwrite.

Let M/A denote each logical target's main/alternate physical storage; initial
flipper state is main. Gbuffers use the prepared current side and do not alter
the postprocess flip ledger.

| Stage | Native RT1 current | Candidate RT1 current | RT3 current/history |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| prepare fullscreen RT1+RT7 | A | A | M holds previous c2 history |
| gbuffers / deferred input | A | A | M |
| deferred RT1+RT4 output | M | M | M |
| composite: RT1 mip generation, then RT1 output | A | A | M |
| composite1 RT1 output | M | M | M |
| composite2: reads RT1 M + previous RT3 M | A | M (no RT1 output/flip) | A holds new c2 result |
| final image reads | RT1 A | RT3 A | same new shared clamped result |
| final native swap-copy from this pair | RT1 A→M and RT3 A→M | RT3 A→M only | next c2 samples previous M |

This predicted native swap behavior follows exact FinalPassRenderer construction:
every final flipped no-clear target gains a SwapPass; cleared targets are skipped.
Removing RT1's fifth output/flip removes its swap-copy membership. There is no
new compensating RT1 copy in this source graph. Other targets' swaps are unchanged.
Actual graph/GL calls still need root observation. No copy is manually suppressed.

Native DOF-off formats of RT1 and RT3 are both R11F_G11F_B10F. Native composite
generates mips only on input RT1 M, then writes A; c1 writes M; c2 writes A.
Thus final's native sampled RT1 A has not acquired mip filtering this frame.
RT3 has no mip-generation request. Exact Iris initializes noninteger target
textures with linear filtering and clamp-to-edge; final resets both sides' min
filters after each frame. This gives matching source filter histories without
assuming implicit derivatives select LOD0. Candidate preserves each direct,
CAS, chromatic, FXAA or included sampling expression; only sampler identity changes.

DOF-on would generate RT1 A mips in c1, then overwrite A in c2; implicit final
reads can retain that mip/filter history. The candidate therefore uses native
paths for every DOF-on case. AA0 has no RT3 store and remains native. DEBUG_MODE
also remains native. Other native options stay present. C2 retains its original
motion-before-TAA order, clamp, RT3 history and alpha expressions; final vertex
exposure/RT6 and all dimension wrappers remain unchanged. RT3 M is not aliased
to its simultaneously written A during c2.

## Conditions and checks actually run

Candidate compile-time predicate is `AA_TYPE > 0 && !defined DOF && !defined
DEBUG_MODE`; it removes an attachment/store/flip before graph construction.
It has no distance units or spatial transition: changes are whole-graph selection
at Apply/reload. Source fallback retains native AA0/DOF/debug branches. Runtime
admission is narrower: only the already-retained 100-option native map (AA2,
DOF false, debug false) and exact pinned renderer/source are initially qualified.
Every unqualified map/version selects original; no option is changed for admission.

`python3 .../makeup-mrt-r1/audit.py` passed source/ZIP pin checks, 48 actual archive
conditional fixtures across four dimension wrappers and AA0/1/2/3, DOF and debug,
disabled transparent source and native-fallback equality, absent duplicate c2
store, include-wide final sampler alias coverage, exact two-member edits, license/
native option preservation, and the symbolic physical flip/mip/swap model.
The exact count is in audit.json. C preprocessing uses clang; **this is not Iris
parsing, GLSL compilation or driver rendering**. One initial fixture incorrectly
treated unchanged clear metadata as a sampled RT1 use; it failed, was narrowed
to actual sampler declaration/texture calls, and rerun. No runtime gate was weakened.
Fresh javap inspected the exact pinned JAR without running Gradle or a client.

## Root acceptance and remaining boundaries

The emitted fixed graph is not connected to the current MakeUp mod uniform or
selection recipe. Ordinary catalog/source binding does not admit it. The staged
ROOT_INTEGRATION_PROPOSAL.md identifies a separate explicit experiment/transaction
with PERFORMANCE-only ownership and native original restoration on Off, QUALITY,
Cancel, mismatch or unsupported state. A shader-side late branch cannot restore
the original graph and must never be presented as this connection.

Root next needs one finite untimed original/control/candidate graph check: loaded
archive and actual native100 options, successful actual preprocessed/driver sources,
prepare full viewport/draw/RT1 output, c2 original [1,3] versus candidate [3],
physical previous/current RT3 join, final current sampler, format/extents/levels,
actual effective sampler state, blend/color masks/dither/conversion equivalence,
swap lists/calls and no candidate RT1 compensating copy. Compare actual original
RT1/RT3 packed output equality and matched control/candidate final pixels/history;
source strings alone do not establish attachment conversion equality.
Reload/resize/first-frame/dimension/DH/PBR still/motion and restoration are separate
runtime boundaries. The original native map includes PBR-related options and DH
water, but those bytes do not prove runtime compatibility.

Only after graph/quality admission should root measure matched baseline and
candidate GPU c2/final-copy time and total-rendering throughput, with repeats
under the project's short-sanity policy and source/observer jobs stopped. A draw
buffer removed in source does not establish actual saved GPU work or useful speed.
No gain, quality parity, supported integration or project completion is claimed.

Frozen `actual-launch-argfiles/packagedMainRunVmArgs.txt` line17 contains the exact required R5 argument, and the generated original file mtime was **12:13:56.537906 UTC**, inside this launch. The populated current-session class-load log corroborates execution. This real counterexample demonstrates missing argfile coverage, not a wrong class-origin path. The guard correctly refused under its existing implementation; no in-run exception or weakening occurred.

`last-admission-failure.json` retains **Wrong class log session** at **12:14:22.550654 UTC**. Neither `admission.json` nor `interaction-admitted.json` exists. The helper's later origin/world/runtime predicates were never reached by this admission; the scoped findings below come from separate raw-file review.

The staged synthetic test at `packaged-interaction-readiness-r1/test_packaged_interaction.py` line46 constructs a direct-Xlog argv. Its four methods/36 negative fixture cases, saved test log and handback do not cover the actual launcher form. I inspected these artifacts without rerunning tests. The prior report already labels them synthetic, so their passing status must retain that scope.

The private installed JAR hashes to **7ecf471e1750c1ed933718480b3224b5038e2c073a7cad3a856f00ad877e3428**, equals current `build/libs/shaderlod-0.1.0-dev.jar`, and contains no ShaderLOD dev members. Actual prelaunch schema is `sourceSet=packagedMain`, `loadedMods=[]`, `systemProperties={}`, 106 classpath entries and the exact private expected JAR. Loader debug lines76–77/212–213 discover that private JAR as main `shaderlod` 0.1.0-dev.

The only `shaderlod_dev` warning is the exact saved-world **version 0.1.0 → MISSING** CommonHooks context in both logs, not a loaded development module. This establishes noDev at inspected JAR/registration/class-origin scope, not a production-launcher compatibility claim.

Actual console ordering: world join line1828 at 05:14:08, overworld pipeline creation 1830 at 05:14:08, main runtime 2117 at 05:14:09 local/Pacific. Main runtime reports original MakeUp, patchedPackName=false, shadersInUse=true, fallback=false, DH=false, enabled=true and PERFORMANCE. `ShaderLodCommands.reportRuntime` requires a nonnull client level. OpenGL lines740–742 identify **Apple M3 Max / Apple / 4.1 Metal - 91.7**. These are actual driver/pipeline/runtime clues; no visible rendered frame, complete option map, backend execution/counts or native viewport/focus proof follows from them.

There is no `session/ui-focus-once.json`, focus/input/inspect receipt or runtime screenshot. Session inventory contains only `owner.json` and `console.log`. The sole image under the entire R5 tree is the copied world's `icon.png`, which is not a captured runtime frame. Parent `release.json` likewise records focusAttempted=false and screenshots=[]. **On/Off/Quality/Cancel, UI text, cache transitions, quality and performance are unverified.** No timing denominator, frame comparison, physical-read saving or full-controls result exists.

Preparation fingerprints are not a postrun unchanged-settings certificate: four entries differ from `profile/prepared.json` after the run—`iris.properties`, `fml.toml`, saved `level.dat`, and missing MakeUp shader-options sidecar. Expected/actual hashes are retained in checks.json. No complete loaded-options map was captured. These differences are qualified evidence, not silently excused gate checks; the original shader ZIP and JAR remain identical.

# MakeUp early native alpha R1 — independent source admission

**ADMIT one fresh, untimed driver attempt for the frozen native100 world0
terrain sources, conditional on separate frozen linkage admission.** No source
counterexample was found in this selected Minecraft 1.21.1 path. This admits an
experiment, not driver compilation, effective activation, quality or gain.
Actual sampler/core/alpha/source joins remain required before cost acceptance.

Reviewer `/root/makeup_early_alpha_source_review` read the latest active Goal,
EVALUATION, frozen shader handback/report, original archive and actual original
ShaderPrinter sources. Scope excludes LIVE linkage staging. Ownership is only
this report and new ignored `makeup-early-alpha-r1/review-shader/`; parent owns
integration, builds, client/GPU and project checkpoints. No shared resource was
used, and no existing stage/check program was rerun.

## Concrete source findings

Independent checks read zip bytes, extracted files and pins directly. Original
0036da17…19db8, control842608ef…246897 and candidatee57635cc…87915 match the
frozen release. Both arms change only native
`shaders/world0/gbuffers_terrain.fsh`, redirecting its original include. The four
added members are three private GLSL copies and NOTICE. Inverse entry/body,
shadow and fog transformations recover complete original bytes. Every vertex,
property, license and credit remains original. No quality option, native
preset, render target, history, distance transition or geometry changed.

Actual raw original ShaderPrinter exports, independently checked against their
recorded pins, show SOLID081 has no rejection and CUTOUT082 rejects late with
`!(iris_FragData0.a > iris_currentAlphaTest)`. The latter fetches atlas*tint,
executes shadow/gloss/fog, clamps all components, writes output, then discards.
The selected native alpha has no intervening assignment after the atlas*tint
fetch until the final vec4 clamp. The candidate passes precisely
`clamp(blockColor.a,0,1)` to its private predicate at that same atlas value.
The clamp preserves native coverage, including tint alpha; the source encodes
no alpha reference, operator or bias. Native output and late rejection remain.

Skipped native work contains local arithmetic and texture reads. The selected
graph has no output before rejection, depth write, image write, atomics or
barrier. End-portal changes RGB through arithmetic only; material gloss has no
texture operation. The atlas stays before the new divergence. The selected
candidate graph has exactly one source early discard, no later direct implicit
lookup and no derivative operation. Calls after rejection reach only the four
audited shadow/fog helpers.

The predicate stub returns false; absent adaptation rejects nothing. A false
private uniform prevents early discard and dispatches all four helpers through
original implicit calls with original arguments. Its branch condition is
uniform across the draw. Pinned `AlphaTest.toExpression` independently confirms
ALWAYS returns disabled-test text before consulting the reference, and retains
its special sentinel/NEVER behavior. Source-only approval does not assert that
the future bridge handles those cases correctly: native ALWAYS/SOLID must stay
inactive, and actual CUTOUT must use the original consuming reference and rule.

## Surviving-sample derivative contract

The helper replacements preserve coordinates, comparison input, tap offsets,
shadow branches and fog arithmetic. Shadowtex0/1 use explicit shadow LOD0;
shadowcolor0 and gaux4 use explicit texture LOD0 on the enabled branch. Soft and
pixelated source variants retain their complete native bodies except dispatch.
Selected soft colored shadows retain all native comparisons and conditional
color reads; darkness retains its native fog-read bypass.

I independently regenerated bytecode from the actual runtime Iris jar
`3e3f94d2…182e83` (1.8.12 snapshot/local). All ten distinct classes in the
owner's three sampler/texture/shadow dumps match byte-for-byte. Additional
fresh `AlphaTest` and `CommonTransformer` inspection confirms original-rule
emission and shadow2DLod→textureLod wrapping. This is pinned implementation
provenance, not physical GL observation.

Native depth mip directives are false. Native uppercase shadowColor0Mipmap is
not assumed recognized: pinned color SamplingSettings defaults to mipmap=false
and nearest=false. The selected properties have no override for these four
bindings. Only colortex0/1 have native post mip directives. `GlSampler` gives
matching MIN/MAG for unmipped depth samplers, `ShadowRenderTargets` selects that
sampler, and `ShadowRenderer.configureSampler` gives matching MIN/MAG while
adding mip work only when requested. Noninteger RenderTarget allocates level0
and sets both filters LINEAR. Color/render-target sampler bindings use no
sampler override; `SamplerBinding` converts null to sampler0 and binds it
explicitly. No inspected constructor enables anisotropy.

Under the same base-level, nonmipped, isotropic and matching MIN/MAG contract,
LOD0 preserves native sample filtering without requiring discarded neighbors.
The [Khronos extension specification](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/extensions/ARB/ARB_shader_texture_lod.txt)
defines explicit LOD in divergent flow and limits its anisotropic behavior.
**Physical anisotropy above1, different MIN/MAG, mip use, base-level change or a
custom binding must block activation.** An analytical counterexample is retained
in checks.json: for two texels[0,1], MIN=NEAREST/MAG=LINEAR and a minifying sample
at u=.5, native picks one texel while explicit LOD0 can blend to.5. No-mips alone
is insufficient. This is a contract counterexample, not a detected runtime bug.

## Unsupported selections and driver boundary

This review admits only the pinned native100 world0/noDH Minecraft1.21.1 terrain
path. Existing entity BLACK_ENTITY_FIX/lightning/flame/weather alpha branches
are separate, untouched entry points and cannot be redirected into this
predicate. Other dimensions, translucent/water/hand/shadow/DH and changed native
options remain original/inactive until separately admitted. DH's native
pre-atlas transition discard and newer IRIS_INLINE_GLINT's post-atlas
`mc_sampleGlint()` create different derivative/coverage graphs; no generic
approval covers them. Unknown sources, presets, versions, PBR/resource
combinations or samplers cannot inherit selected-path acceptance.

One parent-owned driver admission should prove fresh actual transformed
CUTOUT/source/archive identity, exact original/native100 options, shader in use
without fallback, main-mod PERFORMANCE/core linkage, private uniform active in
the actual consuming program, original native alpha reference/rule, retained
late test, native ALWAYS inactive, and physical four-sampler contract including
bound sampler object/filters/levels/comparison/anisotropy/no overrides. Source
comments or CPU config/readbacks do not establish these joins. Off/QUALITY and
missing/unknown bridge must restore original behavior. The actual native wrapper
must have no new externally visible skipped side effects.

Existing three fragment parses are only owner's parser evidence. Original
standalone GLSL120 integer-attribute and compatibility anonymous-member link
failures remain preserved unchanged; this review ran no replacement GLSL links.
Actual Apple driver execution remains unverified. Then inspect representative
cutouts, distant shadow/fog/water cues and motion before the bounded early cost
screen. Control isolates changed sampling/integration overhead; untouched
original and original-return remain absolute denominators. The earlier terrain
3.945292ms/n74 query domain includes other work and is no isolated removable
fragment budget. No quality or speed claim is made.

Independent reproducible evidence: `review-shader/check_independent.py`,
`checks.json`, `pinned-api-comparison.json` and `independent-api.javap.txt` under

# MakeUp merged submission renderer R1

**Frozen, UNINTEGRATED and DEFERRED.** This is a concrete current-pass copy-first renderer prototype, not a retained improvement or completed product. Parent selected the cheaper same-region adjacent-quad coalescer for the next GPU experiment. No active source, build, client, Goal or STATUS was changed by this worker.

## Concrete implementation

Six new Java files and one mixin resource are staged in `renderer/staged/`. `integration.patch` adds only those files; bootstrap registration and program/source linkage are separate integration work.

`MergedChunkRendererMixin` intercepts the pinned renderer after native begin, framebuffer selection and camera matrices. It admits only world SOLID/CUTOUT, with exact original program ownership, expected framebuffer and matching current Iris vertex stride. Translucent and shadows use the existing renderer. The original program remains the default; sibling `MergedProgramAccess` retains the paired derivative. Admission failure leaves the untouched original draw loop available.

For each native nonempty region, the prototype calls the same `fillCommandBuffer` with the same list iterator/camera/pass/face-culling values. It snapshots every native count, base vertex and index pointer in order. `MergePlan` requires positive complete quad counts, zero shared-IBO pointers, nonnegative bases, finite offsets, known mutable VBO byte extents divisible by stride, and every referenced vertex within that extent. It copies the smallest enclosing referenced vertex interval from each regional VBO, using `CommandList.copyBufferSubData`, into a distinct page-aligned range of an orphaned temporary VBO. Source arena gaps inside that interval are copied as inert bytes; only the exact original commands fetch vertices. It never interprets, edits or draws those gaps.

Destination starts and padded ends align to 4096 vertices. Rebased bases equal `destinationStart + nativeBase − sourceStart`. Counts and zero index pointers remain unchanged; the existing native shared sequential quad IBO remains bound. One native multidraw submits the same ordered subdraw sequence for the pass. Nothing crosses SOLID/CUTOUT program boundaries. Limits are 256 MiB including padding, 16,777,216 vertices, 4096 region ranges/pages and 1,048,576 commands; exceeding a limit falls back without dropping geometry. Empty/single-region passes remain native.

`MergedBuffers` owns only reusable GL storage identities, a native tessellation, command allocation and a TBO texture. All copied geometry, commands and offset words are rebuilt from the current pass; no native regions, lists, visibility or mesh bytes survive as reusable data. Orphaning/storage, copies, padding, table assembly/upload, program transitions, state queries/restoration and shader lookup are candidate costs. The native renderer delete hook releases owned buffers/VAO/texture/command memory. Shared native IBO ownership is unchanged.

The agreed shader ABI is a `GL_RGBA32UI` texture buffer, with each page containing exact `Float.floatToRawIntBits(nativeRegionOffset.xyz)` and zero W. `gl_VertexID >> 12` selects the page. Sibling shader code substitutes only the regional offset and caches one fetch per vertex. Native local section IDs and every compressed vertex byte are retained. Names: `shaderlod_makeup_region_offsets`, `shaderlod_makeup_merged_input_enabled`, `shaderlod_makeup_region_page_count`.

Sibling `MergeUniforms.Activation` owns derivative program setup, actual sampler admission, TBO unit binding and original-program restoration. The false-input control explicitly runs the same native regional assembly/draw loop on the derivative interface; it has no copies or enabled lookup. It therefore is a shader-interface/program-transition control, **not** a control isolating copy or lookup cost. The untouched original is the performance denominator. Candidate activation closes before native pass cleanup; `activeProgram` returns to original. `BufferBindings` restores the entry VAO/EBO/ARRAY/COPY_READ/COPY_WRITE bindings and invalidates Sodium's cache through the pinned `GlStateTracker.clear()` accessor. Its bytecode only invalidates handles; it does not mutate GL state. No depth/blend/FBO raster override is introduced by the renderer.

## Lifetime and state challenge

Fresh independently generated `independent-pinned-iris.javap.txt` confirms the renderer behavior used by the handoff: CompositeRenderer constructs outputs against the pre-pass read set and flips each selected target; RT samplers select physical main/alternate from the supplied set. FinalPassRenderer creates copies only for final-flipped targets absent from the clear list. Thus omitting c2 RT1 removes its fifth flip and predicted final RT1 copy, while RT3's read-main/write-alternate/history-copy path is unchanged. This is source construction evidence, not observed calls.

The missing-next-frame RT1 history objection has a source answer: prepare writes RT1 before geometry/deferred/postprocessing, followed by deferred, composite and c1. Candidate c2 still reads the same current RT1 main image; c2 no longer leaves a new RT1 alternate image for final. Final instead reads the new RT3 alternate image. The next prepare overwrites RT1 alternate before the normal chain samples it. RT3 previous-history main and current-write alternate remain distinct; the final alias occurs only in final, so it cannot redirect c2's TAA neighborhood or previous-frame reads. First frame, reload and resize do not add a source read of the discarded RT1 result. Initial contents and actual complete overwrite remain driver checks.

The repeated-final-mip objection also has a bounded source answer: composite generates mips on RT1 main, then writes alternate; c1 writes main; c2 native writes alternate. DOF-off has no RT1-alternate mip generation and final requests none. RT3 has no mip request. RenderTarget initializes noninteger min/mag filters to LINEAR and wraps to CLAMP_TO_EDGE; FinalPassRenderer resets both sides' min filters to LINEAR each normal final return. Existing lower levels on RT1 main are therefore not evidence that the native final alternate samples them. This argument does not assume implicit texture derivatives equal LOD0. DOF-on changes the mip history and is correctly excluded.

Formats and allocation metadata remain native: RT1/RT3 both R11F_G11F_B10F in the qualified DOF-off branch, both no-clear, no native scale/size/flip override. Final alpha remains 1; c2 preserves the shared vec4 result and alpha. No shader image-store or texture-barrier path is introduced. CompositeRenderer disables blend unless a native override is present; the only bounded property blend override is DH water, not c2/final. Its existing compute barrier condition is independent of the removed attachment. FullScreenQuadRenderer disables depth and draws the native quad; this alone does **not** certify live cull/scissor/color-mask/dither state or full viewport coverage.

Independent read-only audit by `tuner_repair`, 2026-10-16. No existing root

MakeUpShadowRuntime.own(program,pipeline,pack,epoch); the native multi-draw wrapper
enters reflection and shadow scopes, queries current state, runs the contracts,
executes native draw, and revokes both shadow permissions in finally. The owner
record certifies the registered program/pipeline/pack epoch, not mutable sampler
parameters or texture storage. Frame/source readiness and lifecycle generation
do not advance on arbitrary GL sampler/texture mutation.

Pinned Iris1.8.12 ProgramSamplers.update iterates SamplerBinding.update; its
updateSampler binds the stored sampler ID and current texture supplier ID. The
optional notifier is a supplier-binding update listener, not a certificate for
all sampler/texture parameter changes. IrisRenderSystem's private samplers[]
array merely avoids redundant binds of the same requested ID. Its
samplerParameteri/f/iv implementations directly invoke GL33 without changing
a parameter generation. Direct GL calls elsewhere can bypass the binding
array. Neither it nor GlSampler's ID proves current compare/filter/wrap/LOD/
bias/aniso or texture format/base/dimensions. IDs can remain unchanged across
parameter mutation and do not certify storage lifetime.

Existing DepthSamplerViews accesses SodiumShader.samplers →
ProgramSamplers.samplerBindings → SamplerBinding unit/type. Photon priming uses
that to enumerate touched units, then still observes actual bindings for
save/restore. It supplies no immutable effective-state snapshot or mutation
epoch. Sildur/Bliss sampler-holder wrappers alter/delegate narrowly named
registration calls, not all subsequent GL writes. PBR prefix certificates carry
atlas/image/storage epochs for their own consuming images; they cannot be
reused as native shadow0/shadow1/color0 sampler certificates.

EarlyAlphaSourceCache still reads full selected/original/state/helper/dependency
content fingerprints per lookup, then can skip its unchanged validator. Its key
contains owners/options/core/queue/world/lifecycle/resources; it contains no GL
state supplier. AdapterRuntimeBinding.snapshot likewise reports declaration/
source/options/layout availability, explicitly not actual linked consumption.
Neither is a substitute for current GL state, and no weakening of their full
fingerprints is proposed.

A cross-draw certificate would require verified mutation coverage for effective
sampler units/bindings, sampler parameter writes, texture storage/base/format/
size and ID lifetime in addition to existing source/world/queue/core guards.

## Native algorithm and index identity

Actual Sodium 0.6.13 bytecode exposes `MultiDrawBatch.pElementPointer`, `pElementCount`, `pBaseVertex`, `size`, and `capacity()`. Pointer slots are 8 bytes in the admitted runtime; count/base slots are 4 bytes. The fill has two returns. The injector targets **RETURN ordinal 1**, the terminal assembly return; ordinal 0 is the empty-iterator return. The native render loop calls fill at bytecode offset 133, then `getIndexBufferSize()` at 163 and `ensureCapacity()` at 166. Native max-count scanning therefore sees merged counts and native shared-index growth remains intact. [Actual API bytecode](../../dev/logs/cross-shader-performance-r2/makeup-quad-coalescer-r1/implementation/api/DefaultChunkRenderer.javap.txt).

The actual native INTEGER index writer emits `[0, 1, 2, 2, 3, 0] + 4q` for quad q. If the first command has base B and 6Q indices, the following command can merge only when its base is `B + 4Q`. Its first indexed vertex then equals the next native index in the larger command. Quad periodicity preserves every ordered index-plus-base reference and triangle, including `gl_VertexID`, for repeated adjacent merges. No command reordering or vertex rewrite is involved. Nonadjacent gaps remain separate.

The implementation requires pointer 0, positive counts divisible by 6, nonnegative signed base vertices and signed vertex-end bounds. It checks size/capacity, pointer stride/alignment/address end bounds before reading. Any custom pointer, malformed count or unsupported base in a batch leaves the whole batch untouched. Summation uses long arithmetic and checked integer addition. A conservative native byte-allocation guard prevents creating a merged command above `(Integer.MAX_VALUE / 24 - 16384) * 6` indices: native first growth reserves the requested quads plus 16,384 and stores 24 bytes per quad. This guard does not change geometry or split/repack meshes. It does not fix pre-existing native extreme-buffer overflow behavior. Native index growth and memory cost may increase with a larger merged maximum and must be charged to the candidate.

They have no `gl_DrawID`, `gl_PrimitiveID`, `gl_BaseVertex`, `gl_BaseInstance` or `gl_InstanceID` dependence. `_draw_id = a_LightAndData[3]` is native vertex-encoded section identity; its region translation remains unchanged. ## Native later-growth safety before mutation

Keep the actual terminal fill `RETURN ordinal 1`; no current-capacity accessor or tracking is needed. Native max-count scanning and shared-index growth still happen afterward. Preflight computes the exact planned maximum while validating every command; any malformed/custom-index command or request outside the proven domain leaves the entire batch untouched before the first write. Compaction retains adjacent-only grouping and the original ordered native index-plus-base stream.

For integer indices let `Q = floor(INT_MAX / 24) = 89,478,485` quads and `R = min(floor(Q / 2), Q − 16,384) = 44,739,242`. Every candidate command is bounded by `6R = 268,435,452` indices. For any nonnegative current native capacity `p` and admitted request `r ≤ R`: if `r ≤ p`, native ensureCapacity does not grow; otherwise `p < r ≤ R`, so `2p < 2R ≤ Q` and `r + 16,384 ≤ Q`. Therefore native `next = min(max(2p, r + 16,384), typeMax)` has safe int intermediates and `24 × next ≤ INT_MAX`. Each later batch repeats this proof. The actual pinned INTEGER domain has `typeMax = INT_MAX / 4`, above R.

The independent fixture invokes actual Sodium private getNextSize and public ensureCapacity using a CommandList proxy which records allocateStorage's argument and stops before mapping/GL. It reproduces the review's old capacity `50,016,384`, request `50,020,000` quads, native next `100,032,768`, and actual wrapped allocation `−1,894,180,864` bytes. The production request bound rejects that case. A late unsafe third command proves the earlier merge remains unwritten. This prevents newly introduced overflow; it does not repair a native failure in a batch that falls back untouched.

Entry is `shaders/world0/deferred.fsh` →
`common/deferred_fragment.glsl` → `lib/ao.glsl:dbao`. The unchanged native
attenuation is `pow(clamp(linearDepth * 1.6, 0, 1), nativeExponent)`.
The new condition reads this already computed result and requires exact
`ao_att == 1.0`. Only then does it leave `final_ao=1.0` and omit `dbao`.
The branch is before the whole AO call, including its center fetch, ten paired
depth fetches and five cosine/sine offset evaluations at native AOSTEPS5.
No texture read, derivative or new reconstruction is added to the classifier.
Unskipped pixels execute the exact original `mix(dbao(dither),1,ao_att)`.

`linearDepth` is MakeUp's native normalized `ld(depth)` value, computed as
`2*near/(far+near-depth*(far-near))`; it is **not world distance in blocks**.
For finite positive native exponents its existing clamp saturates at normalized
`ld >= .625`. The candidate compares the final native attenuation, rather than
reconstructing a block cutoff or changing the clamp. The native transition is
unchanged: full native AO runs throughout every non-saturated part of it.
Presets share the same exact-zero policy because no quality approximation is
introduced; no new preset-dependent threshold is necessary.

Eligibility requires private option one, actual integer
`shaderlodBridgeVersion=2`, `shaderlodEnabled=1`, `shaderlodPreset` in 0–2,
and positive native `near` with `far > near`. This matches current
`CoreUniformFrame`/`LodPreset`: Balanced0, Performance1, Aggressive2, Quality3.
Option zero, core Off, Quality3, missing uniforms (zero initialization), unknown
presets or wrong bridge retain full native AO. Source excludes Nether, End,
unknown dimensions, DH and VOXY. Those paths, and AO-off, preprocess exactly
to original. These exclusions are unverified compatibility boundaries, not
claims that their AO is impossible to optimize.

For finite native inputs the original mix at attenuation1 returns exactly1;
the elision preserves its AO lighting contribution. The proof assumes valid
finite native depth/offset samples and selected native strength. It does not
establish equivalence for corrupt/NaN native AO data. No near AO or nonzero
distant occlusion is deliberately removed. Actual renderer SIMD execution
and driver work savings remain measurement questions.

The full-work control has the identical common-stage branch source and a
helper option default of zero. The compiler may fold away its classifier;
this is a native-work/graph control, not a measured isolator for classification
overhead. Absolute original comparisons must charge all candidate overhead.
Restoration selects the untouched original, never an inverse approximation.

## Current-frame ABI and range association

| Field | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `shaderlod_makeup_region_offsets` | Scalar `usamplerBuffer`, integer GL texture-buffer target, `GL_RGBA32UI`; one 16-byte texel per staging page. |
| Texel xyz | `Float.floatToRawIntBits` of the **same three float arguments** as native `SodiumShader.setRegionOffset`, for this current region/pass/frame; no recomputation from camera/origin in shader. |
| Texel w | Zero reserved word; no metadata or temporal meaning. |
| `shaderlod_makeup_merged_input_enabled` | Scalar GL_BOOL; linked default false. False uses original `u_RegionOffset`, with zero new fetches. |
| `shaderlod_makeup_region_page_count` | Scalar GL_INT, positive admitted table extent; default zero. |
| Association | `page = gl_VertexID >> 12`; copied region starts and padded extents align to 4096 vertices. Each covered page stores that region's same offset words. |

Renderer sibling owns the native vertex stride, command/byte copies, buffer binding, range admission and dynamic binder. For each nonempty region it copies the native interval `[minReferencedBase, maxReferencedEnd)` unchanged, pads its destination extent to a page, and rebases each original base vertex by `destinationStart - sourceMin`. Counts, sequential index pointer/type/content, local draw IDs, command order and SOLID-before-CUTOUT order are preserved. Native indexed `gl_VertexID` then addresses the same destination bytes and the corresponding page. The entire eligible pass must be admitted before any copied draw: finite original offsets; native stride/byte alignment; original sequential quad commands and index coverage; nonnegative signed index-plus-base; source bounds; disjoint page-aligned destinations; complete table coverage; capacity and texture-buffer limits. Proposed renderer cap is 256 MiB staging and at most 16,777,216 vertices / 4096 pages; actual vertex stride may make the byte cap tighter. Use checked wide arithmetic before narrowing to signed GLsizei/int. Padding is never indexed.

Adjacent regional origins 0 and 128 blocks with identical compressed local vertices/local draw IDs require different table offsets. An unaligned boundary at staging vertex4095 assigns region A's4094 and region B's4095 to the same page and is therefore invalid; padding moves the second region to4096. NaN/infinite offsets are rejected: GLSL finite `uintBitsToFloat` preserves representation, whereas nonfinite results are unspecified. Signed zero and finite subnormal words are included in the source model. The basis is [GLSL 3.30 specification](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/gl/GLSLangSpec.3.30.pdf), sections7.1/8.3/8.7; integer `texelFetch` uses no derivatives or implicit sampling LOD. Indexed base-vertex association must also be checked on the actual driver. A malformed-range shader guard cannot repair invalid merged geometry: reject the complete candidate pass and execute native regional submissions instead.

The [OpenGL3.3 core specification](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/gl/glspec33.core.pdf), sections2.8.3/2.11.7 and table3.15, defines the drawing-command index exposed as `gl_VertexID`, base-vertex array addressing and RGBA32UI buffer format. This is a concrete core3.3 path; no DrawID/SSBO/compute/MDI facility is assumed.

Offset units are original camera-relative blocks. ## Behavior and quality budget

Native `fastRaymarch` uses `exp2(i + dither)` exploration then binary refinement,
with hidden-surface classification and `no_hidden_steps < 3` fallback in the same
ten-iteration loop. Reducing iterations and scaling stride cannot preserve those
decisions merely by preserving ray extent. This experiment therefore uses the
authorized safer fade/skip alternative rather than claiming equivalent sample
reduction.

`SHADERLOD_MAKEUP_WATER_SSR=0` is the default and selects the complete original
`reflection_calc` text. The disabled GLSL excludes the added helper. Pack member
bytes still contain option/preprocessor additions; the off function and original
ray function are exact original text. The source checks distinguish those facts.

When enabled with native `REFLECTION_SLIDER=2`, radial distance comes from
`dot(fragpos, fragpos)` in Minecraft block units. Pinned
`src/position_vertex_water.glsl` sets `fragposition = (gl_ModelViewMatrix *
gl_Vertex).xyz`; the fragment passes that originating camera/view-relative value.
Full reflection weight remains through 96 blocks, smoothstep fades it to zero
through 160, and the far branch returns before any SSR depth or scene fetch.
Options clamp start to zero and end to at least start + 1 block. There is no
moving random mask; camera motion still needs temporal quality inspection.

Every retained trace uses original search/refinement math, ten iterations and
original exponential ray coverage. Fade pixels retain the full trace budget.
Beyond the end, the existing `water_shader` fallback receives reflection alpha
zero and uses its precomputed sky/cloud color; `infinite=1` follows the native
offscreen sun-glint path. This removes distant on-screen reflected geometry.
Sun-glint differences at the fade end must be inspected because the native
`infinite` value describes ray outcome rather than the blend weight. Native
reflection-off/projected-image controls remain original code and ignore the new
option. No medium/far shortened raytrace kernels are implemented.

## Explicit sampling and near limits

The enabled helper replaces only its copied depth fetch with
`texture2DLod(depthtex1, ..., 0.0)`; the active reflection function fetches
`texture2DLod(gaux1, ..., 0.0)`. This avoids reliance on implicit derivatives
across the nonuniform distance skip. Both operations occur after the skip;
there is no discarded unconditional trace or late branch hiding it.

Pinned MakeUp declares `gaux1Format = R11F_G11F_B10F` in
`common/final_fragment.glsl`; it requests mipmaps only for colortex0/colortex1
in composite/composite1. No `gaux1MipmapEnabled` or `colortex4MipmapEnabled`
directive exists. Depthtex1 has no mipmap declaration. All eight water entry
points enable `GL_ARB_shader_texture_lod` in GLSL 120.

Static inspection of the actual pinned Iris 1.8.12 jar (SHA256
`3e3f94d2d5cdcb8145c4385d521974aa2d8669b2cc212351f70cf06488182e83`)
with `javap -c -p` shows `RenderTarget.setupTexture` initializes noninteger
targets with GL_LINEAR (9729) for MIN/MAG and CLAMP_TO_EDGE (33071), allocating
level zero. `DepthTexture` allocates level zero with GL_NEAREST (9728) MIN/MAG
and CLAMP_TO_EDGE. `ProgramDirectives` starts mipmappedBuffers empty and fills
it only from enabled pack directives. Combined with the pinned declarations,
this supports base-level sampling equivalence as a source inference. The enabled
near path is **not byte-identical**: its fetch syntax differs. Exact driver
pixels, sampler bindings and near motion still require a runtime comparison.
